**Flow Management**

- Excessive flow rates may result in air not being fully saturated
- Downstream pressure fluctuations can result in pumping mechanism with air moving from circuit back into vaporiser chamber → saturated gas can be forced back through the vaporizer inlet port and enter the bypass channel resulting in increased agent delivery

Management:

- Baffles and wicks increase surface area and liquid/gas interface ensuring air saturation
- One-way valve at the outflow of the vaporizer can prevent back flow  

Temperature Management

The SVP of volatile agents increases non-linearly as temperature increases. Temperature changes can occur through:

- Changes in ambient temperature 
- ↓ from latent heat loss of vaporisation → liquid in vaporiser cooling

This is controlled through:

- The use of a heat sink and materials with high conductivity and heat capacitance allowing the vaporiser to buffer ambient temperature fluctuations and buffer heat loss through latent vaporisation. 
- Temperature Compensation with bimetallic strip → which changes shape/bends in response to temperature changes changing the splitting ratio of air bypassing and entering the vapour chamber
